title: TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated SAW) - Band 30 (2300 MHz) for Public Safety Band Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Stefan Richter

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated SAW) filter targeting Band 30 (2300 MHz) for Public Safety Band Filter. The filter is designed on 128° YX LiNbO3 substrate with a target center frequency of 4104.5 MHz and bandwidth of 88.0 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Public Safety Band Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated SAW)
- Frequency Band: Band 30 (2300 MHz)
- Application: Public Safety Band Filter
- Substrate: 128° YX LiNbO3
- Package: CSP (Chip Scale Package)
- Design Tool: CST Studio Suite 2024
- Design Center: Osaka Design Center

This specification applies to all variants of the TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated SAW) design targeting Band 30 (2300 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       4104.5 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       88.0 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.9 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 23.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 50.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 28.0 dB
Q Factor:               7569
Temperature Coefficient:-25.5 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.5 x 1.1 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   5
Electrode Material:     W
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open CST Studio Suite 2024 and load the TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated SAW) template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: 128° YX LiNbO3 with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 4104.5 MHz, BW 88.0 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.9 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (CSP (Chip Scale Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, 128° YX LiNbO3).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 12314 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.9 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 23.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 132 MHz offset >= 50.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 6 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 13.1 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +29 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 1000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 98%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-06-05
Devices Tested:         48
Insertion Loss (meas):  2.57 dB
Return Loss (meas):     24.8 dB
Rejection (meas):       52.5 dB
Isolation (meas):       33.1 dB
Q Factor (meas):        7569
Group Delay Variation:  7.3 ns
Power Handling:         +27 dBm
Die Yield:              92.6%

Result Classification:  FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The TC-SAW (Temperature Compensated SAW) design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 30 (2300 MHz).
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Simulation-to-measurement correlation was within 3% for all key parameters.
e) No delamination observed after 1000-cycle thermal shock test.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Optimize resonator geometry to reduce insertion loss by ~0.3 dB.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Escalate to advanced materials team for alternative piezoelectric stack.
